decisions.question: a + b infix operator calls: Scala desugars to a.+(b) — a real method call. But operators are overwhelmingly stdlib/primitive (+, *, ::, map...) and there is no symbol table to filter user operators. Recommend: DECLARED LIMITATION (operator calls not emitted as Calls edges).
decisions.resolution: DECLARED LIMITATION (2026-08-27): infix operator calls are not emitted as Calls edges. Operators are overwhelmingly stdlib/primitive and there is no symbol table to filter user operators — emitting them would flood the graph with noise.

decisions.question: export scala.concurrent.duration.* — the export relationship kind is NOT EMITTED (pattern flag only). Recommend: DECLARED LIMITATION (consistent with kotlin S5 / groovy S3).
decisions.resolution: DECLARED LIMITATION (2026-08-27): export declarations are NOT EMITTED as export relationships (pattern flag only) — consistent with kotlin S5 / groovy S3.

decisions.question: Parameterless method access without parens (xs.length, s.x) parses as field_expression — method vs field is indistinguishable without a symbol table. Recommend: fold into G8 — emit Uses on the RECEIVER only, never guess the selector kind.
decisions.resolution: RULED (2026-08-27): parameterless/nullary access (xs.length) folds into G8 — emit Uses on the RECEIVER only; the selector kind (method vs field) is never guessed without a symbol table.

decisions.question: XML literals: the grammar declares them but the analyzer ignores them entirely. Recommend: internal_silent (XML literal bodies are out of scope; embedding them would fabricate symbols).
decisions.resolution: INTERNAL SILENT (2026-08-27): XML literals are out of scope; the grammar declares them but the analyzer ignores them — embedding would fabricate symbols.

decisions.question: (1, "a") tuple literal: an expression, not a declaration. Recommend: internal_silent (destructured locals are not symbols — consistent with kotlin S3).
decisions.resolution: INTERNAL SILENT (2026-08-27): tuple literals and destructured locals are not symbols — consistent with kotlin S3.

decisions.question: Scala 3 macros: quote/splice expressions — handleCall already skips callees starting with a quote char (dotty-corpus fix). Recommend: internal_silent (macro AST manipulation is out of scope).
decisions.resolution: INTERNAL SILENT (2026-08-27): Scala 3 macros (quote/splice) — handleCall already skips quoted callees; macro expansion is out of scope.

decisions.question: Implementing an ABSTRACT member needs no `override` keyword in Scala (required only for CONCRETE base members). The analyzer's override post-pass was keyworded-only — keywordless abstract implementations emitted nothing. Are they overrides?
decisions.resolution: Yes. Two-corpus gate wave 2026-09 (cats-effect Semaphore/Queue/AtomicCell): keywordless exact-signature implementations of in-file abstract members are verified overrides @1.0/exact-in-file. The oracle additionally had to start counting abstract `function_declaration` members (the shared member-variable guard was swallowing them). No guessing tier for implicit pairs — overloads must never pair.

decisions.question: Keyworded overrides without a companion index guessed the FIRST supertype (ConcurrentImpl.get -> CommonImpl.get @0.5) even when the real declaring ancestor (AtomicCell) is in-file and an intermediate (CommonImpl) does not declare the method. Resolve the true ancestor?
decisions.resolution: Yes. Two-corpus gate wave 2026-09: keyworded methods now first resolve the verified in-file declaring ancestor by exact name+parameter-type signature BFS (emit @1.0/exact-in-file); the companion/first-supertype guess tiers run only when no in-file ancestor declares it.

decisions.question: `private[effect] def tag` parsed as plain `private` — hiding it from exports AND making the analyzer treat the member as non-overridable (26 keywordless IO subclasses implement IO.tag). Correct handling?
decisions.resolution: Scope-qualified private/protected (private[pkg], protected[pkg]) is visible and overridable within its scope — modeled as package-scoped visibility (never exported, still inheritable). Bare private stays private. Two-corpus gate wave 2026-09 (cats-effect IO.scala: 26 tag implementations).

decisions.node_type: anonymous class body (new Runnable { ... } — instance_expression + template_body)
decisions.question: M37.21 #610 JD18 family lesson (java finding, scala shares the gap): methods inside anonymous bodies attributed to the enclosing class (run -> Service) with no anonymous symbol — the contains graph leaked the body's members into the enclosing type.
decisions.resolution: Mirror the kotlin/java family convention: anonymous_<SuperName> Class symbol (generic supertypes collapse to the head name, bracketed args stripped; noise name, never leaks into the index) owned by the enclosing type, pushed as the walk parent so body members attribute to the anonymous type (contains anonymous_Runnable -> run). Oracle mirror: deriveTreeEdges registers the synthetic anonymous declaration (methods + supertype parent) so scala overrides truth covers anonymous-body members (cats-effect 91 -> 8 unexplained; the remaining 8 are the documented ~>/compound-instantiates shapes). Fixture pins in java/anonymous-and-multihop-overrides; scala fixture pending in the scala wave.

decisions.node_type: oracle override emission when same-named companions pool into one decls entry (scala)
decisions.question: cats-effect IsEq.scala: decls['IsEq'] unions the trait's methods (declares toProp) with the object's parents (extends IsEqLowPriorityImplicits which also declares toProp) — pooled emission fabricated `IsEq.toProp -> IsEqLowPriorityImplicits.toProp`, an override that exists on NEITHER real type (analyzer resolves per-symbol and emits nothing). 1 unexplained @200.
decisions.resolution: Per-occurrence provenance for scala: every declaration registers its OWN method set + its OWN extends_clause parents (occMethods/occSigs/occParents); scala override emission walks occurrence keys exactly (no name fallback — a name fallback would reintroduce the conflation). Transitive BFS depth-10 and sigCompatible (hasTypeVar bracket-aware) preserved. Companion-union pooling stays truth for every other family.

decisions.question: M49 #741 CONV-S-1 (family-wide blind-spot sweep, C7 class): did scala detect Spring? Probe at HEAD measured detectedFrameworks=[] for a Spring Boot import while java ("spring"), kotlin ("Spring Boot"/"Spring Framework") and groovy ("spring") all detected it — scala was the only JVM language blind to the dominant enterprise ecosystem. Root cause: the S1.23 root-prefix list was sound but incomplete (Play, Akka, Spark, Cats Effect, ZIO, http4s, Slick, FS2, ScalaTest only).
decisions.resolution: Added root-prefix entries org.springframework.boot -> "Spring Boot", org.springframework -> "Spring Framework", plus the JSON/HTTP libraries a mixed JVM shop actually imports: com.fasterxml.jackson -> "Jackson", com.github.plokhotnyuk.jsoniter_scala -> "jsoniter-scala", com.softwaremill.sttp -> "sttp". Matching stays root-prefix, so user code that merely contains a framework root (com.mycompany.springframework.*, mycats.*, org.springlike.*) still detects nothing. Naming follows kotlin's for the same ecosystem and scala's own Title-Case list style.
decisions.evidence: fixture scala/framework-detection (5 expects + 9 forbids); mutants scala/spring-detection-loss and scala/framework-substring-fabrication must each die on that fixture alone; reproduction + negative control in script/m14/tmp/sc-frameworks-probe.ts.
decisions.familyDivergence: RECORDED, NOT RESOLVED: java and groovy emit the lowercase key "spring" for the same ecosystem while kotlin and scala emit "Spring Boot"/"Spring Framework". One analyzer must not unilaterally rename a consumer-visible family payload, so scala matches kotlin and the divergence is left for a family ruling (the family-parity gate's construct set does not currently cover framework names).
decisions.runFixturesGap: FIXED IN THE SAME WAVE: `expectFrameworks` is a must-include list, so a detector that over-matches passed every framework fixture — the go fixture's header already CLAIMED an "exact detected set" the runner could not check. run-fixtures.ts now supports `forbidFrameworks`, which is what makes the negative direction of this fixture (and the substring mutant) load-bearing.

decisions.status: OPEN — the class is derived and load-bearing; ONE defect remains
decisions.question: `extension (x: T) { def name = ... }` publishes `uses name -> T`. The receiver lives on an `extension_definition` ANCESTOR and the published name is the receiver node's WHOLE TEXT, with exactly one trailing `?` stripped (Scala 3's `String.?(...)`). After the first oracle read the receiver off a field of the function and published only the first type identifier, adjudication on scala3's repl/ and project/ produced eight analyzer-only rows — `List[T]` published as `List[T]`, not `List`. Corrected, the class is load-bearing (removing it drops 25 of 27 extra rows on a 70-file scala3 draw). But a residual remains and is NOT closed.
decisions.residual: scala3 400 files: 17,423 truth, 17,398 covered (99.9%), MISSING 25, uses-UNEXPLAINED 7. cats-effect 400 files: 9,642/9,642, MISSING 0, UNEXPLAINED 2 — effectively clean, and it contains no `extension (` at all. Every residual row is in a file with MULTIPLE Scala 3 `extension` blocks closed by `end extension` (ExtractSemanticDB.scala, Long.scala, Nullables.scala, Decorators.scala, Scala3.scala), and in each the two sides name DIFFERENT receivers: e.g. Decorators.scala has nine `extension` blocks and the sides resolve `String` against `Iterator[Symbol]`; Long.scala misses `uses isWhole -> Long` entirely. Two further UNEXPLAINED rows are `overrides` on `anonymous_BuildFrom`, a different label and a separate question.
decisions.hypothesis_not_conclusion: The suspected cause is that Scala 3's `end extension` block form is indentation-based, so with several blocks in one object the walk to the NEAREST `extension_definition` ancestor can reach the wrong block. This is NOT established: it needs a parse dump of one of those files showing which extension_definition actually encloses the def, and until that is done it is a hypothesis. It is recorded as a hypothesis precisely because the alternative — that the ANALYZER is right and the oracle is wrong — has not been excluded either.
decisions.what_is_proven: The class is DERIVED, LOAD-BEARING, and correct on every shape probed directly: `extension [T](xs: List[T])` publishes the whole text; a trailing `?` is stripped once; a `def` (as opposed to a `val`/`type`) is excluded because its receiver belongs to the method signature. Five further rules of the OTHER uses class are each load-bearing: interpolation (14 truth-only), the self-receiver field (7+9), the call-fn skip (148 analyzer-only), the write-span gate (5), and the capitalized-receiver guard (104).

decisions.node_type: function_definition (local definitions) and object/class expressions (anonymous owners) — the `contains` class
decisions.status: OPEN — the oracle is INCOMPLETE, and the incompleteness is the finding
decisions.question: `contains` has one emission site: every symbol with an `ownerName` publishes `owner contains member`. The first scala contains oracle implemented only ONE of the three owner kinds scala has — a TYPE owning its members — and the 95 unexplained rows on a 60-file cats-effect draw are the other two: a METHOD owning its local definitions, and an ANONYMOUS object/class that is itself contained and contains its own members.
decisions.the_three_owner_kinds_measured: (1) TYPE owns its members: `C contains constructor/val/var/def/type/nested`. Derived and correct. (2) METHOD owns its local definitions: `readLineWithCharsetImpl contains decodeNext/decodeNextLoop/loop`, and `MonadCancelOps_ contains !>` — a method with a symbolic name. The analyzer attributes a local def to the enclosing function, as `f->loc` showed in a direct probe. (3) ANONYMOUS object/class: the analyzer names it `anonymous_<Owner>.<Name>` and both contains it in its owner and publishes its members — `anonymous_Console.MapKConsole`, `anonymous_WorkStealingThreadPoolMetrics`, `anonymous_WorkerThreadMetrics`, `anonymous_GenTemporalLaws`.
decisions.state: cats-effect 60: truth 1,947/1,947 covered, MISSING 0, UNEXPLAINED 95 (5.2%). scala3 60: truth 3,968/3,969, MISSING 1, UNEXPLAINED 140 (4.2%). The MISSING=0 side is the trustworthy half: every member the ORACLE derives, the analyzer publishes. The 95/140 are the oracle's incompleteness, not analyzer fabrications — and they are NOT load-bearing for the analyzer, they are a gap in the instrument. `contains` is therefore NOT closed and must not be reported as covered.
decisions.two_oracle_bugs_already_fixed_here: Both were the same class of mistake as the kotlin oracles — reading the wrong child list or one grammar shape. (a) `val`/`var` in a class parameter are ANONYMOUS tokens, so scanning `namedChild` found no fields at all: 112 unexplained rows, every one a constructor `val`/`var`. (b) The parameters arrive in TWO shapes — `class C(val a: Int)` wraps them in `arguments`, while `class C protected (val a: Int)` puts class_parameter DIRECTLY under class_parameters, because an access modifier between the name and the paren drops the wrapper. Reading only the wrapped form found 0 of IORuntimeBuilder's 9 fields.
decisions.next_action: Extend deriveScalaContainsTruth to owner kinds (2) and (3), re-measure, and only then run the load-bearing battery. A `contains` oracle that derives a subset cannot prove the analyzer's extra rows are fabrications, so the 95/140 must be closed BEFORE any mutant is trusted on this label — the kotlin lesson that a partial oracle reports a green lane is exactly the failure this label is currently in.
